headword: {公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}

definitions.explanation: The wife of a duke, or a woman who holds the rank of duke in her own right. The highest female title in the European peerage system below royalty.

examples.japanese: {公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}が{挨拶|あいさつ}をした。
{公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}は{慈善活動|じぜんかつどう}で{知|し}られている。
examples.english: The duchess is known for her charitable activities.

examples.japanese: {小説|しょうせつ}の{主人公|しゅじんこう}は{若|わか}い{公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}で、{社交界|しゃこうかい}での{陰謀|いんぼう}に{巻|ま}き{込|こ}まれていく。
examples.english: The novel's protagonist is a young duchess who becomes entangled in the intrigues of high society.

notes:
Composed of {公爵|こうしゃく} (duke) and {夫人|ふじん} (wife, lady). This title belongs to the European peerage system and is encountered primarily in historical contexts, novels, and news about European aristocracy. Japan had its own {公爵|こうしゃく} rank in the {華族|かぞく} (nobility) system from 1884 to 1947.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}の{称号|しょうごう}: the title of duchess
- {公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}として{知|し}られる: known as a duchess
- {公爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}の{肖像画|しょうぞうが}: portrait of a duchess

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {公爵|こうしゃく}: duke — the male title
- {侯爵夫人|こうしゃくふじん}: marchioness — wife of a marquis; note same reading こうしゃくふじん but written with {侯|こう}
- {伯爵夫人|はくしゃくふじん}: countess — wife of a count/earl
